1.3.3.1-f26.accuracy_reason: The lines are Orestes' words in his madness in a Latin version of Euripides (Orestes 255 ff.), and Electra's reply follows in the text.

1.3.3.1-f29.accuracy_reason: Seneca, Hercules Furens 313–314, reads 'quod nimis miseri volunt / hoc facile credunt'; Burton changed 'volunt' to 'timent'.

1.3.3.1-f36.accuracy_reason: The note says correctly that 'reminiscentia' is Plato's anamnesis, the soul recollecting knowledge it had before birth.

1.3.3.1-f9.accuracy_reason: In De tranquillitate animi 17.10, Seneca gives 'nullum magnum ingenium sine mixtura dementiae fuit' and credits it to Aristotle. Burton does leave out 'fuit'.
